title: Pole order at a point of a product of integer powers of polynomials
statement:
Let $K$ be a field, $T$ an indeterminate, $K[T]$ the polynomial ring [def-weil-polynomial-ring], $K(T)$ the field of rational functions with its reduced presentations [def-weil-rational-function-field], $c\in K$, and let $m_c(P)$ be the multiplicity of $c$ as a root of $P\in K[T]$ [def-weil-root-multiplicity]. Then:

1. For nonzero $P,Q\in K[T]$: $m_c(P)=0$ if and only if $P(c)\neq0$; $m_c(PQ)=m_c(P)+m_c(Q)$; and $m_c\bigl(u\,(T-c)\bigr)=1$ for every $u\in K^\times$, in particular $m_c(1-c^{-1}T)=1$ when $c\neq0$.

2. Let $P_0,\ldots,P_n\in K[T]$ be nonzero, let $e_0,\ldots,e_n$ be integers, let $R=\prod_{j=0}^nP_j^{e_j}\in K(T)$, which is nonzero, let $R=N/D$ be its reduced presentation ($D$ monic, $\gcd(N,D)=1$), and put

$$
\nu=\sum_{j=0}^ne_j\,m_c(P_j)\in\mathbf Z.
$$

Then $m_c(N)-m_c(D)=\nu$, and at most one of $m_c(N)$, $m_c(D)$ is nonzero. Consequently, for an integer $m\geq1$, $R$ has a pole of order exactly $m$ at $T=c$ in the sense of [def-weil-rational-function-pole-order] if and only if $\nu=-m$, and $R$ is regular at $T=c$ if and only if $\nu\geq0$.

3. In particular, if for one index $j_0$ one has $e_{j_0}=-1$ and $m_c(P_{j_0})=1$, and $P_j(c)\neq0$ for every $j\neq j_0$, then $R=\prod_{j=0}^nP_j^{e_j}$ has a pole of order exactly $1$ at $T=c$.

source.place: ## Proof, second to fourth paragraphs: 'the order of vanishing of $P_i$ at $T=c^{-1}$ is the number of $r$ with $\alpha_{i,r}=c$' and 'As $P_0$ occurs with exponent $(-1)^{0+1}=-1$, $Z(X_0,T)$ has a pole of order exactly $1$ at $T=1$' (likewise for $P_{2d}$ and $T=q^{-d}$): the bookkeeping of root multiplicities in the product $\prod P_i^{(-1)^{i+1}}$ that these sentences take for granted; also literature/blueprint/master/blueprint/sec-zeta-weil/sk-thm-betti/_section.md, ## Proof: 'to read off the pole orders one must exclude cancellation against $N_\ell$ and further multiplicity from other factors of $D_\ell$'

mathlib_searches.query: grep -rhn 'theorem rootMultiplicity_mul\b\|theorem rootMultiplicity_eq_zero\b\|theorem rootMultiplicity_pos\b\|theorem rootMultiplicity_X_sub_C_self\|theorem rootMultiplicity_C\b' Mathlib/Algebra/Polynomial/Div.lean Mathlib/Algebra/Polynomial/RingDivision.lean
mathlib_searches.results: rootMultiplicity_mul (hpq : p * q ≠ 0) : rootMultiplicity x (p * q) = rootMultiplicity x p + rootMultiplicity x q (RingDivision.lean 291); rootMultiplicity_eq_zero (h : ¬IsRoot p x) (Div.lean 629); rootMultiplicity_pos (hp : p ≠ 0) : 0 < rootMultiplicity x p ↔ IsRoot p x (Div.lean 637); rootMultiplicity_X_sub_C_self : rootMultiplicity x (X - C x) = 1 (RingDivision.lean 167); rootMultiplicity_C (r a : R) : rootMultiplicity a (C r) = 0 (Div.lean 536)
mathlib_searches.verdict: match for clause 1 (the three polynomial facts; the last from rootMultiplicity_mul with rootMultiplicity_C and rootMultiplicity_X_sub_C_self); clauses 2 and 3 are not stated for RatFunc
